correctedState: Confirmed, with one qualification the finding should carry. There is no per-task isolation control anywhere on the scheduled-automation path: not in AutomationMatcherSchema (packages/shared/src/automations/schemas.ts:168-186, which carries permissionMode at :178 and nothing else), not in either create/update surface (shared/src/automations/management.ts, session-tools-core/src/handlers/automation-management.ts), not in the Electron editor model (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/automations/types.ts), and not in the launch call (SessionManager.executePromptAutomation -> createSession at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:18582). Under defaults a scheduled run therefore executes in the workspace working directory against uncommitted changes, matching only the FIRST half of the doc's Note. The qualification: the fork owns the machinery, it is just not reachable per task. worktree.bgIsolation exists as a GLOBAL settings key (packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts) and, when set to "worktree", blocks Edit/Write in the main checkout for every session including scheduled ones (pre-tool-use.ts:934,:948) — but it creates no worktree; the agent must then call the Pi-only EnterWorktree tool. That key's default is "none" in this fork against Claude's documented "worktree", by a reason recorded in the module note (worktree-settings.ts:9-16): the release valve is Pi-only, so a Claude- or Codex-backed session would meet an unliftable write block. So 'nothing lets a scheduled automation request a worktree' is exact for a per-task toggle, and slightly overstated as an absolute — a Pi-backed run whose prompt instructs EnterWorktree, or a user who opts the whole install into bgIsolation, can approximate it. Closing the gap is an additive matcher field (e.g. worktree?: boolean) plumbed from the schema through management.ts, the editor and createSession into a WorktreeLeaseService lease; the per-child precedent already exists at SessionManager.ts:4900-4902.
